item.title: Mini Crackme — 2026-09-05 (Windows x86-64)
item.description:
Challenge: `ecx` holds a 32-bit unsigned integer (Windows x64 calling convention, first arg in `ecx`). Find the value of `ecx` that makes `check` return 1.
check: imul eax, ecx, 0x1F ; eax = x * 31 and eax, 0xFF ; keep only the low byte of the product cmp eax, 0x51 ; compare to target byte jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret
Answer: ecx = 0x8F (143). `imul eax, ecx, 0x1F` multiplies x by 31, and `and eax, 0xFF` keeps only the low 8 bits, so the check depends only on x mod 256. Solving (31*x) mod 256 == 0x51 requires 31's modular inverse mod 256, which is 223; multiplying both sides gives x = 0x51*223 mod 256 = 143. Passing ecx=143 gives 31*143=4433=0x1151, whose low byte is 0x51, so check returns 1.
